title: 〜も〜ば〜も / 〜も〜なら〜も
romaji: mo … ba … mo / mo … nara … mo
meaning: "both ~ and ~", "not only ~ but also ~" — listing two items of the same kind.
simpleExplanation: Two parallel clauses, each marked with も, joined by a ば- or なら-form. The two items must point the same way — both good or both bad.
whenUsed: Praising or criticising something on two counts at once.
formation: N + も + V-ば + N + も + V
N + も + い-adj-ければ + N + も + adj
N + も + な-adj / N + なら + N + も

diagram.translation: It's cheap, and the food is good too.

examples.ja: この店は値段も安ければ、味もいい。
examples.reading: このみせはねだんもやすければ、あじもいい。
examples.en: This place is cheap and the food is good too.

examples.ja: 彼は英語も話せれば、中国語も話せる。
examples.reading: かれはえいごもはなせれば、ちゅうごくごもはなせる。
examples.en: He speaks both English and Chinese.

examples.ja: 彼女は歌も上手なら、ダンスも上手だ。
examples.reading: かのじょはうたもじょうずなら、ダンスもじょうずだ。
examples.en: She's good at singing and at dancing too.

examples.ja: 人生にはいい時もあれば、悪い時もある。
examples.reading: じんせいにはいいときもあれば、わるいときもある。
examples.en: In life there are good times and bad times alike.

similarGrammar.difference: Also 'not only… but also', but the two items may differ in nature. 〜も〜ば〜も stresses that both share the same evaluation.
Casual listing of reasons; less structured.
Casual, non-exhaustive examples; no parallel evaluation.

commonMistakes.wrong: この店は安ければ、味も悪い。
commonMistakes.right: この店は安いが、味は悪い。
commonMistakes.why: The two items must share the same evaluation. Cheap (good) and bad taste (bad) do not match, so use a contrast.

commonMistakes.wrong: 英語が話せれば、中国語も話せる。(as this pattern)
commonMistakes.right: 英語も話せれば、中国語も話せる。
commonMistakes.why: The first item needs も; with が the sentence becomes a plain conditional 'if he can speak English…'.
な-adjectives use なら (or であれば), not ければ.

usageNotes: Some/others: 賛成する人もいれば、反対する人もいる.
In writing, なら can be replaced with であれば.
The verb after the second も is often the same as or similar to the first.
jlptTips: The first blank after Noun + も needs a ば-form; check the choices for 〜ば / 〜ければ / なら.
Both halves must be positive or both negative; a mismatch signals a different pattern.
The set phrase 〜もいれば〜もいる is common in 読解 to describe a variety of people.
